title: Introduce a structured logger (replace console.error, add server-fn error logging)
description: Recurring 'no logger yet' gap flagged across reviews: src/db/client.ts pool 'error' handler console.error dumps the full pg client object (noisy in e2e output); P1 review flagged server-function handlers log nothing and env-validation errors lack context. Add a small structured logger, replace the console.error in db/client with logged error.message, and add log-and-rethrow at the server-fn boundary for observability.
design: Logger library: pino + pino-pretty (chosen after sweeping pino/winston/bunyan/roarr/tslog/consola/evlog/morgan/log4js — pino is the most-adopted in-category structured JSON logger, fastest, with child() context + redact). Shape: server-only src/lib/logger.ts; JSON to stdout in prod (Coolify/container aggregation), pino-pretty transport in dev; redact configured for token/secret fields (e.g. authorization, CF_EMAIL_TOKEN, invite codes). Scope: (1) the logger module; (2) replace db/client pool 'error' console.error with logger.error(err.message ...); (3) log-and-rethrow at the server-fn boundary. This is the base layer; wide-events/canonical-log-line request middleware is a separate follow-up that builds on it.
notes: Re-scope (per spec-conformance review): design item (3) 'log-and-rethrow at the server-fn boundary' is NOT in this bead — it lands in gf-fwi.13 (minimal error-logging request middleware, the production observability baseline), which gf-fwi.12 then extends into wide-events. This bead delivers (1) the pino logger module + (2) the db/client pool-error replacement only. Note: db/client logs the whole error via pino's {err} serializer ({type,message,stack,code}), richer than the literal 'error.message' the description names — captures pg error codes (ECONNRESET, 57P01) that message alone drops.
close_reason: Structured pino logger delivered: src/lib/logger.ts (prod JSON / dev pino-pretty tree-shaken from prod bundle, redact for secret fields, LOG_LEVEL from process.env with allow-list validation + warn-on-invalid). db/client pool-error handler now logs via pino's {err} serializer (captures error.code) instead of console.error. resolveLevel unit-tested. title: Harden first-admin bootstrap against the concurrent-signup race
description: The first-user→admin bootstrap (src/lib/auth/server.ts createAuth) is a TOCTOU race: on a brand-new DB, two concurrent signups can both read hasUsers()===false before either commits, so both bypass the invite gate AND both get role='admin'. Accepted for now per decision 0013 (the gate is intentionally off for the first signup) and realistically unreachable for a single-operator self-host that signs up once right after deploy. Flagged by codex (P1) + review agents during gf-fwi.2.3. Fully closing it is architectural: the gate (plugin before-hook) and the admin-grant (better-auth user.create hook) live in separate hooks/requests, so a robust fix needs an out-of-band bootstrap (env-designated admin / one-time setup token) or a schema-backed single-winner (sentinel row + advisory lock). Address before exposing open/public registration.
design: FIX (env-designated admin, chosen 2026-06-17): INITIAL_ADMIN_EMAIL designates the bootstrap admin. createAuth(db, {initialAdminEmail?}) — defaults to env, overridable for tests. user.create.before: if adminExists() return; else require newUser.email===designated (lowercased) and grant role=admin, else throw APIError('FORBIDDEN',{code:'INVITE_REQUIRED'}). Gate enabled:adminExists (open only until first admin). DOUBLE-ADMIN RACE CLOSED: better-auth lowercases email pre-insert (sign-up.mjs:164) + UNIQUE email column = single-winner; two concurrent designated signups -> second insert fails -> one admin, no case-variant escape. Non-designated signups during bootstrap rejected with the same INVITE_REQUIRED surface as the closed gate (no bootstrap-state leak). RESIDUAL (accepted, inherent to open-gate model; Direction 2 seed+always-on-gate would eliminate): a sub-ms window where a NON-admin could pass the open gate then have adminExists flip true mid-flight -> created as a regular un-invited user. No privilege escalation. Fail-closed when INITIAL_ADMIN_EMAIL unset: every signup rejected until designated. Tests: invite-gate.integration (bootstrap, case-insensitive match, non-designated reject, gate-close, undesignated fail-closed); session/email-flows/password-reset integration + e2e webServer wired with INITIAL_ADMIN_EMAIL=manager.
notes: Source: gf-fwi.2.3 review. See the documented window in src/lib/auth/server.ts databaseHooks.user.create.before.
close_reason: Hardened first-admin bootstrap against the concurrent-signup TOCTOU race via env-designated admin (INITIAL_ADMIN_EMAIL). Only the designated email may register on a fresh DB and becomes admin; better-auth lowercases email pre-insert + the UNIQUE email column is the single-winner guard, so concurrent designated signups can't both claim admin (double-admin race CLOSED). Non-designated signups during the bootstrap window are rejected with the same INVITE_REQUIRED surface as the closed gate (no bootstrap-state leak); unset INITIAL_ADMIN_EMAIL fails closed. Gate enabled:adminExists (open only until first admin). Accepted residual (user chose env-designated over seed+always-on-gate): a sub-ms non-privileged gate-bypass window. Verified: 33 auth integration tests (incl. concurrent-winner, case-insensitive both sides, reopen-on-removal, fail-closed-undesignated) + 8 e2e (env->gate path end-to-end). Docs 0009/0013/spec-0001 updated. Follow-up gf-utf: constrain role column / 'admin' magic string.

title: Server-fn/request error-logging middleware (observability baseline)
description: gf-fwi.10 added the pino logger, but nothing logs server-fn/request errors yet: a thrown server function leaves no structured, contextual log line (only Nitro's default stderr). Add the minimal global request middleware that catches errors from Start-handled requests (serverFn + router), logs them via the logger with request context, and rethrows. This is the production observability baseline — do not deploy to prod without server-error logging. NOT the full wide-events model (gf-fwi.12 extends this).
design: Add the Start instance (no src/start.ts yet) and register a global request middleware via createStart({ requestMiddleware: [errorLog] }). errorLog = createMiddleware({type:'request'}).server(async ({ request, pathname, next, handlerType, serverFnMeta }) => try { return await next() } catch (err) { logger.error({ err, method, pathname, handlerType, fn: serverFnMeta?.name }, 'request error'); throw err }). Uses pino's {err} serializer (captures error.code). This is the SAME middleware gf-fwi.12 extends into wide-events (ALS field accumulation + one canonical log line per request + reqId from cf-ray) — foundation here, ambitious layer there. Refs installed @tanstack/start-client-core 1.170 createMiddleware (request type; handlerType serverFn|router; registered via createStart requestMiddleware).
close_reason: Error-logging request middleware delivered: src/start.ts (Start instance + global errorLogger request middleware logging THROWN server-fn/router errors via dynamically-imported pino then rethrow; CSRF re-added since defining start.ts disables Start's auto server-fn CSRF). handle-request-error.ts (log-and-rethrow helper, logger injected for client-safety) + is-loggable-error.ts (skips redirect/notFound control flow + sub-5xx Responses), both unit-tested. 5xx-Response-RESULT logging deferred to gf-fwi.12 (owns it, trigger note added). Reviewed 2 iterations (codex + 5 agents, all converged); 58 tests + typecheck/lint/build green; client bundle verified pino-free.

title: Extract reusable layouts (header, footer, app shell) under components/layouts
description:
The root document (src/routes/__root.tsx RootDocument) inlines the html shell plus a global header (logo link, SignOutButton, ThemeSwitcher). There is no footer, the header renders identically on every surface (landing, auth, app), the auth pages have their own centered layout (src/routes/_auth/route.tsx), and route components each inline their own main wrapper.

WHAT: introduce src/components/layouts/ with composable layout pieces. Extract the header into layouts/header.tsx and move the SignOutButton into the header/layouts (the header is its only consumer). Add a footer (layouts/footer.tsx). Factor an app shell layout (header + main + footer) that __root composes. Consider distinct layouts for public/auth vs the gated app if the chrome should differ by context (marketing landing vs app chrome). Keep the data-hydrated marker and Providers wiring in __root.

WHY: a single home for header/footer/shell so layout changes are not scattered across __root and per-route main wrappers, and so public vs app surfaces can present different chrome.
notes: Move SignOutButton (src/components/sign-out-button.tsx + sign-out-button.test.tsx) into the header/layouts since the header is its only consumer; it already self-hides when signed out via authClient.useSession (gf-4k5). _auth/route.tsx centered auth layout is a candidate to move under layouts/. User scaffolded the empty src/components/layouts/ dir. Touches __root.tsx — coordinate with the errors bead.

title: Consolidate global error + not-found components under components/errors
description:
root-error.tsx (the RootError boundary wired as errorComponent in src/routes/__root.tsx) lives loose under src/components/, and there is no global not-found UI: __root sets errorComponent but no notFoundComponent or defaultNotFoundComponent, so a thrown notFound falls back to TanStack Router's bare default. The player detail route (src/routes/_app/players/playerId.tsx) carries a one-off inline 'Player not found.' message. is-loggable-error.ts already classifies notFound/redirect as control flow, not errors.

WHAT: move root-error.tsx + root-error.test.tsx into the new src/components/errors/ directory; add a shared not-found component there; wire a defaultNotFoundComponent (and a per-route notFoundComponent where useful) into the root route so a real global 404 UI exists; update the player route to use the shared not-found (via notFound + notFoundComponent, or the shared component) instead of the inline message. Preserve the RootError logging behavior (SSR-inline log + client effect, filtered through is-loggable-error). Import from concrete module paths per the no-barrel rule.

WHY: one home for global error/not-found UI, an actual 404 page, and no duplicated ad-hoc not-found markup.
notes: Refs: router-core/not-found-and-errors skill (notFoundComponent, defaultNotFoundComponent, notFoundMode, CatchBoundary). User scaffolded the empty src/components/errors/ dir. Touches __root.tsx (coordinate with the layouts bead, which also edits __root).

title: Validate runtime role writes from Better Auth /admin/set-role
description:
gf-utf made app-owned role reads/writes typo-safe at compile time (typed column + ADMIN_ROLE const), but the Better Auth admin plugin's runtime /admin/set-role endpoint still accepts ARBITRARY role strings — text({enum}) is TS-only and the plugin writes via its internalAdapter, bypassing drizzle's typed builder. An admin could persist a typo'd/invalid role that the bootstrap probe (eq(user.role,'admin')) would not recognize as admin. Flagged by codex (P2) during gf-utf review.

WHY DEFERRED / NOT URGENT: no consumer exists yet — there is no admin UI and nothing calls set-role, so no code path can currently persist an invalid role (the only writers are the plugin's defaultRole='user' on create and our bootstrap grant 'admin', both valid). The failure mode is also fail-SAFE (a bad role loses admin recognition, doesn't grant it; doesn't reopen the gate). 

WHAT (do this WITH the admin role-management feature, when set-role is first exposed): constrain runtime role writes — wire the admin plugin's access-control /statement model to validate role input against the allowed domain, OR add a multi-role-aware DB CHECK (NOT a plain pgEnum — the plugin stores comma-separated multi-role strings, see gf-utf). Decision 0013 currently keeps a minimal user/admin model with no granular permissions, so revisit that scope here.
notes: Source: gf-utf review (codex P2). Relevant: src/lib/auth/server.ts admin() plugin config (no roles option), src/db/schema.ts role column (text, TS-only enum).

title: Constrain the user.role column + replace the 'admin' magic string
description:
The first-admin gate (gf-fwi.2.7) rests on a stringly-typed value the schema doesn't enforce: src/db/schema.ts role is text() (nullable, unconstrained), and 'admin' is a load-bearing magic string in BOTH the adminExists() probe (eq(user.role,'admin')) and the create-hook grant (role:'admin') in src/lib/auth/server.ts. A typo in the filter would silently make adminExists() always false and REOPEN the bootstrap gate — a security-adjacent failure with no compile-time guard. Flagged independently by the type-design and maintainability reviewers during gf-fwi.2.7 review.

WHAT: constrain role to a typed domain (pgEnum or text({enum:['user','admin']}).$type<Role>()) and replace the scattered 'admin'/'user' literals with a shared const, so a typo becomes a compile error. CAVEAT: the role column is owned by the Better Auth admin plugin (defaults user/admin) — verify the typed column stays compatible with the plugin's reads/writes (it sets role on create and via setRole). Keep the gf-fwi.2.7 behavior identical; this is a type-safety refactor, no behavior change.

WHY DEFERRED FROM gf-fwi.2.7: the column is library-owned and constraining it is a separate schema/migration concern outside that bead's race-hardening scope.
notes: Source: gf-fwi.2.7 review (type-design-analyzer + maintainability-auditor). Files: src/db/schema.ts:143 (role: text()), src/lib/auth/server.ts:50,77 ('admin' literals).
close_reason: Typed the user.role column to the 'user'|'admin' domain via drizzle text({ enum: USER_ROLES }) — TS-only narrowing (verified no migration; column stays plain text so the admin plugin's comma-separated multi-role writes aren't rejected), making a typo'd role filter/grant a compile error. Extracted ADMIN_ROLE const used by the bootstrap probe + grant (src/lib/auth/server.ts); test helper insertUser tightened to UserRole|null. No behavior change (33 auth integration + 138 unit pass). Test 'admin' literals kept as test-as-spec (now typo-safe via the column type). Follow-up gf-thb: validate runtime /admin/set-role writes (no consumer yet; out of scope).

title: Enable Sentry source-map upload + release tagging
description:
gf-yru wired Sentry but deferred source-map upload + release tagging (both are the CI/deploy half of the integration). Today: stack traces in Sentry are minified, and errors aren't associated with a deploy.

WIRED BUT DORMANT (from gf-yru):
- vite.config.ts has the sentryTanstackStart({ authToken: SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN, org: SENTRY_ORG, project: SENTRY_PROJECT }) plugin — no-ops without the token, so it's inert now.
- pnpm-workspace.yaml allowBuilds sets '@sentry/cli': false (its binary does the upload) — flip to true when enabling.
- .env.example documents SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN / SENTRY_ORG / SENTRY_PROJECT (CI-only, build-time, never committed).

WHAT:
1. Provision a Sentry auth token (org+project) as a CI/build secret (never committed).
2. Flip '@sentry/cli': true in pnpm-workspace allowBuilds so its binary builds.
3. Confirm the sentryTanstackStart plugin uploads source maps at build and the dashboard symbolicates client + server stacks.
4. RELEASE tagging: the plugin injects a release when uploading, OR set release explicitly in both Sentry.init (instrument.client/server) from a build var (e.g. git SHA). This closes gf-yru's one partial acceptance item ('release/environment set' — environment is set, release was deferred here).
5. Verify source maps are NOT shipped to the public client bundle (upload-then-delete, the plugin's default).

NOTE: these are BUILD-time vars read via process.env in vite.config (build tooling, not app runtime config), so they correctly do NOT go through t3-env.
acceptance_criteria: Source-map upload runs at build with a CI-provided auth token; client + server stack traces are symbolicated in Sentry; errors are tagged with a release; source maps are not served in the public bundle; @sentry/cli build enabled in allowBuilds.
notes: Deferred from gf-yru (the plugin + env + allowBuilds=false scaffolding already exist; this turns it on). release tagging couples here because the plugin injects it during upload.

title: Wire Sentry into the isomorphic logger + logError seam (server pinoIntegration + client captureException)
description:
gf-vy9 builds an isomorphic pino logger plus a single `logError(cause, message)` primitive that every client/server catch routes through. That primitive is the deliberate upgrade seam for Sentry — this bead plugs Sentry in with no logger rewrite.

WHY: client/SSR errors currently land in pino only (prod client logs reach the user's console with no sink). Sentry gives a real error sink + breadcrumbs/release tracking. Officially supported now, split by runtime along the SSR boundary the logger already respects.

WHAT (two runtime paths, both confirmed in research 2026-06-16):
- Server/SSR (Node): add Sentry's official `pinoIntegration` (in @sentry/node, SDK >=10.18.0, needs enableLogs) so server-side pino logs flow to Sentry automatically — no logger changes. Alt: official @sentry/pino-transport (createSentryPinoTransport) as a pino transport. GOTCHA: pino transports run in a worker thread, so the Sentry transport needs Sentry re-init inside the worker (issue getsentry/sentry-javascript#16723-class). pinoIntegration avoids the worker-thread issue.
- Browser (client): the pino<->Sentry integrations are Node-only. Add Sentry's browser SDK and call Sentry.captureException(cause) INSIDE logError — every client catch already funnels through it, so it's a one-line addition at the single chokepoint.

SCOPE: add @sentry/* deps, init server + browser SDKs (DSN via env, gitignored / deploy-secret — NEVER commit a real DSN), add enableLogs + pinoIntegration server-side, add captureException call inside logError client-side, sample-rate + release/environment config, redaction parity with the logger redact list (password/token/secret/apiKey/inviteCode/authorization/cookie — Sentry beforeSend scrub).

SOURCES: https://docs.sentry.io/platforms/javascript/guides/node/configuration/integrations/pino/ · https://sentry.io/changelog/pino-and-consola-sdk-integrations-for-logs · https://www.npmjs.com/package/pino-sentry-transport
design:
FINAL (option B, decided 2026-06-17): capture via Sentry.captureException in the logError seam, NOT pinoIntegration. Rationale: pinoIntegration needs Sentry auto-instrumentation, which in this ESM project requires --import preload (runs before the app + before t3-env, forces raw env, fragile nitro cp step). captureException sidesteps all of that AND makes server errors first-class Sentry Issues.

CLIENT: logError gates Sentry.captureException(cause) behind import.meta.env.PROD (dev = pino console). DSN via import.meta.env.VITE_SENTRY_DSN (Vite convention, like VITE_LOG_LEVEL); unset -> Vite inlines undefined -> init DCEs to disabled. instrument.client.ts imported first in src/client.tsx; tanstackRouterBrowserTracingIntegration added in router.tsx.

SERVER: logError captureException fires server-side too (prod). instrument.server.ts is a normal BUNDLED module imported at the top of src/server.ts (no --import, no cp) -> it reads env.SENTRY_DSN + env.SENTRY_TRACES_SAMPLE_RATE via t3-env (validated at server boot, where secrets exist; NOT a bootstrap exception). server.ts wraps the handler with wrapFetchWithSentry (catches unhandled request errors); Sentry default integrations catch uncaught/unhandledRejection.

REDACTION: shared scrubSentryPayload (src/integrations/sentry/scrub.ts) wired as beforeSend + beforeSendLog on both inits, mirroring the logger redact list (pino browser can't redact; this is the client parity).

KNOWN GAP (acceptable): server logger.error calls NOT routed through logError (request-log, db pool, invite sweep) don't auto-forward to Sentry; wrapFetchWithSentry still captures thrown request errors. Wire them through a shared helper later if needed.

ENV VALIDATION: runtime/boot via t3-env import (server secrets are runtime-injected, so build-time validation would be wrong). @sentry/cli build script set false in pnpm-workspace allowBuilds (source-map upload deferred).
acceptance_criteria: Client: a handled error in logError reaches Sentry via captureException in prod (stripped in dev). Server: caught errors via logError AND uncaught exceptions/unhandled rejections both reach Sentry (pinoIntegration + default integrations). Switch keys on import.meta.env.PROD, not process.env.NODE_ENV. DSN sourced from env, never committed. Redact parity enforced via beforeSend. Sample rates + release/environment set. Build clean + client bundle leak grep still passes.
notes: Depends on gf-vy9 (logger + logError must exist first). Sentry intentionally OUT of scope for gf-vy9 — that bead only proves the seam. Worker-thread re-init is the one known footgun for the @sentry/pino-transport path; prefer pinoIntegration to sidestep it.
close_reason: Wired Sentry via option B: captureException in the logError seam (PROD-gated, client+server), not pinoIntegration. Added t3-env client/server split (env/{client,server}.ts) with build-enforced markers keeping server var names out of the client bundle; shared scrubSentryPayload (beforeSend+beforeSendLog) mirrors the pino redact list via a single SECRET_KEYS source of truth; server.ts wraps the entry with wrapFetchWithSentry (forwarding request opts); start.ts adds Sentry request/function middleware; router.tsx adds browser tracing; sourcemaps gated on SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN. Follow-up gf-z0b for source-map upload + release tagging.

title: Authenticated password-change flow with 'sign out other devices' option
description: Build an authenticated password-change UI (account/settings page, which doesn't exist yet) using authClient.changePassword({ currentPassword, newPassword, revokeOtherSessions }). Include a 'Sign out other devices?' checkbox driving revokeOtherSessions. This is the user-CHOICE counterpart to the forced revokeSessionsOnPasswordReset on the unauthenticated reset flow (gf-fwi.2.6 Stage 2'-b): reset force-revokes all sessions (compromise recovery), while an authenticated change lets the user decide. changePassword requires the current password, so it only applies to logged-in users.
notes: Better Auth changePassword takes currentPassword + newPassword + revokeOtherSessions (verified in better-auth 1.6 dist). Needs an account-settings surface; likely co-located with gf-7mm (verify-email resend) on that page.

title: Enforce email verification (requireEmailVerification on) + rework signup success/gating
description: Today requireEmailVerification is OFF (server.ts emailAndPassword), so users enter the app unverified and there is no verification UI. This bead OWNS the whole email-verification surface: (1) build the verify-email route/UX (check-your-inbox + authClient.sendVerificationEmail resend, reading the email from the client session so resend only targets the signed-in user), (2) turn requireEmailVerification ON so unverified users cannot sign in, (3) rework the success/gating flow — sign-up no longer auto-enters the app; verify-email becomes the gate; login surfaces EMAIL_NOT_VERIFIED -> route to verify-email/resend (add that case to login's error mapping in src/lib/auth/errors.ts). MUST NOT lock out the bootstrap admin (the original reason the flag is off): auto-verify the first admin or provide a verified bootstrap path.
notes: Deferred from gf-fwi.2.6 Stage 2'-b (the nudge-only verify-email UX was awkward while verification is non-blocking; it belongs with enforcement). Reuses authClient.sendVerificationEmail + the _auth layout. Verification link already works (server.ts emails Better Auth's callback url).

title: Toast notification system (Intent UI sonner + root provider)
description: No toast/notification component exists in src/components/ui. Add Intent UI's sonner-based Toast + a provider in the root (src/providers or __root) for transient user feedback. General-purpose UI infra used app-wide: success ('Career saved', 'Player added'), info, and the prod side of the error-feedback layer (gf-vy9). Part of the agreed hybrid model: inline form/field errors stay inline; toasts cover unexpected/network errors and non-form notifications.
notes: Surfaced while scoping gf-vy9 (client error feedback). Toasts are reusable beyond errors, so tracked separately; gf-vy9 depends on this.
close_reason: Toast system added: Intent UI sonner Toaster (themed via next-themes) mounted in root Providers; shared jsdom matchMedia stub + render test. Unblocks gf-vy9.

title: Client error feedback: dev logger + prod toasts (hybrid with inline validation)
description: Consistent client error-feedback layer (hybrid, agreed 2026-06-16). Expected validation/credential errors stay INLINE on the form/field (already in place: FormError + field errors). Unexpected/network errors go through a reportError(cause, message) helper — dev: logger.error to console; prod: toast (needs gf-78e). Isomorphic logger: make src/lib/logger.ts browser-safe — pino browser:{asObject:true} + an isBrowser guard around the pino-pretty transport; read the client level via import.meta.env (process.env.LOG_LEVEL throws 'process is not defined' in the browser). Keep the redact list so logged causes never carry password/token/inviteCode/cookie/authorization. INFO-DISCLOSURE RULE: user-facing text (inline + toast) is curated strings WE control, keyed by error.code — never echo raw server error.message, exception text, stack, or internal codes; the raw cause goes only to the redacted logger. Nav-blocking: the catch must still return a form-level error (or mark invalid) so a network failure does not let onSubmit run and navigate.
notes: Verified 2026-06-16: invite-plugin messages are safe and login is generic/enumeration-safe, so committed Stage 2' is safe today; sign-up currently echoes error.message ?? fallback — switch to code-keyed curated strings when centralizing the error->message map. OUT OF SCOPE / optional future: global error boundary + window 'unhandledrejection' handler; server log-shipping (/api/log) with hardening (zod payload schema, size cap, rate-limit, allowlist the dynamic logger[level] lookup); PostHog/Sentry captureException (neither SDK in deps). eslint no-console blocks console.* but not logger.*(). Originated from silent-failure-hunter (LOW) in gf-fwi.2.6 Stage 2'.
close_reason: Client error-feedback layer shipped (hybrid). Isomorphic logger (pino browser:{asObject:true} + import.meta.env.SSR guard; client level via VITE_LOG_LEVEL; redact list preserved server-side, browser build can't redact so logError only takes the caught error; logError never throws). logError(cause,message) wired into the 4 auth-form catches (log + keep inline NETWORK_ERROR_MESSAGE, nav still blocked), the sign-out button (toasts SIGN_OUT_FAILED_MESSAGE on failure), and RootError (extracted to src/components/root-error.tsx; curated UNEXPECTED_ERROR_MESSAGE instead of raw error.message — INFO-DISCLOSURE fix; logs on SSR render + client effect). Browser logger is DEV-CONSOLE ergonomics only; prod client+server error sink is Sentry, deferred to gf-yru. /api/log and a logging server fn explicitly rejected. Reviewed 2 iterations; typecheck/lint/unit 95/integration 62/e2e 8/build+leak grep all green.

Chose the landing-at-/ seam: the squad app moved behind the _app guard to /squad (src/routes/_app/squad.tsx, moved verbatim from the deleted _app/index.tsx); an authenticated visitor to / is redirected to /squad (beforeLoad), so login/signup which navigate to / land in the app. SignOutButton now renders on session presence (authClient.useSession) rather than _app route match. title: Optionally verify SMTP credentials/reachability at auth boot
description: assertEmailTransportConfigured (src/lib/email/transport.ts) validates that the email env is SHAPED correctly (CF_EMAIL_TOKEN/SMTP_URL present, EMAIL_FROM when SMTP set) and fails fast in prod when none is configured. It does NOT verify that credentials actually authenticate or the SMTP host is reachable. So a prod deploy with a wrong-but-present CF_EMAIL_TOKEN passes the boot assertion, returns 200 on first signup/reset, and only logs 'email send failed' on the swallowed per-send path (Better Auth's runInBackgroundOrAwait catches callback rejections). Options: call transporter.verify() once at startup behind the same assertion (couples boot to SMTP reachability — a blip blocks deploy, needs a decision), or document that credential validity is covered operationally via alerting on the 'email send failed' error log + a user-facing 'resend' affordance. Surfaced by the gf-fwi.2.5 review cycle (silent-failure-hunter, MEDIUM).
notes: Deferred from gf-fwi.2.5 per fix-vs-defer: needs a network call at boot and a product decision about failing the deploy on a flaky verify.

title: Establish enforced client/server module boundaries (markers + drop dynamic-import workarounds)
description:
gf-fwi.2.2 proved static import + the @tanstack/react-start/server-only marker keeps server code out of the client bundle with NO leak (verified dev AND build, auth route). Import protection is built-in/default-on (v1.168.25); markers cost nothing at runtime (virtual-emptied at build) and turn accidental cross-boundary imports into build errors. Goal: make every single-environment module explicitly marked, then collapse the dynamic-import workarounds that existed only for bundle isolation.

PART A — mark single-environment modules (defensive, no behavior change):
- server-only (import '@tanstack/react-start/server-only'): src/db/client.ts, src/configs/env.ts, src/lib/logger.ts, src/lib/request-log.ts, src/lib/request-context.ts, src/modules/*/services/*.ts. (src/lib/auth/server.ts already marked in gf-fwi.2.2.)
- client-only (import '@tanstack/react-start/client-only'): src/lib/auth/client.ts, src/integrations/next-themes/*, src/lib/analytics.tsx / src/hooks/use-analytics.ts.
- DO NOT mark isomorphic/boundary files: src/modules/*/api/*.ts (createServerFn is client-callable via RPC stub), src/db/schema.ts + drizzle-zod validators (types consumed client-side; runtime value import would break). .server.ts/.client.ts naming is an alternative to markers.

PART B — drop dynamic-import workarounds now made unnecessary by Part A's markers, and remove the matching eslint no-restricted-syntax exemptions:
- src/modules/career|catalog|player/api/*.ts (dynamic import of #/db/client + services) -> static; verify createServerFn handler stripping keeps client clean.
- src/start.ts (dynamic import of logger/request-log/request-context) -> static; createMiddleware is a different boundary than route server.handlers, test carefully.
- src/lib/email.ts (built in gf-fwi.2.4, not yet present) -> build with the marker pattern from the start; no dynamic-import exemption.

Done when: single-env modules are marked, safe dynamic imports are static, corresponding eslint.config.js ignores removed, and typecheck/lint/build + a client-bundle leak grep (.output/public) all pass. Verify BOTH dev (mock warnings) and build (post-tree-shake) per site. Recorded finding: memory tanstack-start-v1-168-static-imports-of-server. Docs: TanStack Start Import Protection.
notes:
gf-fwi.2.6 Stage 3'-a: src/lib/auth/functions.ts (getSessionFn) verifies the static-import + @tanstack/react-start/server-only marker keeps a createServerFn handler's client bundle clean — build + .output/public leak grep show no better-auth/getRequest/secret. Answers Part B's open 'verify createServerFn handler stripping keeps client clean' for the auth fn; the modules/career|catalog|player/api/*.ts dynamic-import refactor + marker Part A remain.

gf-yru env split (2026-06-17): src/configs/env was split into env/server.ts + env/client.ts, BOTH already carrying the server-only/client-only markers (Part A done for those). New Part-A gap surfaced by that review: src/db/client.ts is server-only but lacks its own marker (reached only via dynamic import + server-only callers, so safe today) — add 'import @tanstack/react-start/server-only' to make its server-only contract self-enforcing.

title: Auth hardening for reverse-proxy / production deployment
description: Deferred from gf-fwi.2.2 review (Better Auth security docs). When packaging for self-host behind a reverse proxy (Coolify/Traefik): (1) advanced.ipAddress.ipAddressHeaders — set the trusted proxy IP header so rate-limiting/IP logging can't be spoofed (default reads X-Forwarded-For; Cloudflare = cf-connecting-ip); (2) advanced.trustedProxyHeaders OR dynamic baseURL { allowedHosts } if the instance is reached via multiple hosts (currently static BETTER_AUTH_URL, proxy headers ignored); (3) review trustedOrigins for prod (default trusts baseURL only — do NOT add localhost in prod); (4) consider versioned secret rotation via BETTER_AUTH_SECRETS. Relates to gf-fwi.4 (Docker packaging). Email-enumeration protection is handled in gf-fwi.2.5 (auto-on with requireEmailVerification).

title: Wire React Aria Components navigation to TanStack Router
description: Intent UI components are React Aria Components; their href-based navigation (Link, Menu items, Tabs, Breadcrumbs, Card-as-link) does NOT route through TanStack Router until wired. Nothing is wired yet (no RouterProvider, no createLink, no link.tsx). Needed before any navigation-heavy feature UI is built.
design: (1) Mount React Aria's RouterProvider (from react-aria-components) at the app root (src/router.tsx / __root) wiring navigate -> TanStack Router navigate and useHref -> the router's href builder, so every RAC component with href routes client-side. (2) Add a typed Link via createLink (@tanstack/react-router) wrapping RAC's Link for type-safe to/params/search. (3) Add src/components/ui/link.tsx (Intent UI Link) through that typed createLink. Refs: Intent UI client-side-routing doc (intentui.com/docs/getting-started/client-side-routing); React Aria RouterProvider docs. Note RAC RouterProvider needs the router's navigate signature; TanStack Router exposes it via the router instance.

title: Enrich canonical log line: adopt addRequestFields in services
description: gf-fwi.12 built the addRequestFields/getRequestLog ALS rails but no service consumes them yet, so today's canonical 'request' line carries only method/path/status/durationMs/fn/handlerType — no business context. Realize the wide-events payoff by calling addRequestFields({...}) from career/player services (e.g. careerId, rows-returned, mutation type) so each request's canonical line is queryable on those dimensions. Smoke-verified the line emits end-to-end (router GET / -> one INFO line with reqId, status 200, durationMs).

title: Typed context injection for the request logger (next({context:{log,reqId}}))
description: gf-fwi.12 delivers the request-scoped logger via AsyncLocalStorage (getRequestLog) only. The wide-events design also mentioned typed context injection — next({context:{log,reqId}}) — so server-fn handlers get a typed context.log instead of the ambient getRequestLog(). Deferred from gf-fwi.12 (YAGNI: no server fn consumes context.log yet, and it adds GlobalServerRequestContext type machinery). Implement when a server fn actually wants the typed request logger on its context.

title: Wide-events request middleware (canonical log lines over pino)
description: Observability layer on top of the pino base logger (gf-fwi.10): emit ONE wide, structured 'canonical log line' per request instead of scattered log calls. Grounded in installed @tanstack/start-client-core 1.170 createMiddleware API.
design: Mechanism (verified against installed 1.170 source): use a REQUEST middleware — createMiddleware({type:'request'}).server(async ({request, pathname, next, handlerType, serverFnMeta}) => ...) — registered GLOBALLY via createStart({ requestMiddleware: [loggingMiddleware] }). Key facts: (1) request middleware fires for handlerType 'serverFn' AND 'router' (page/SSR), so one middleware covers both the server-fn data path and page loads — no separate Nitro hook needed for basic coverage. (2) Inputs for fields: raw web Request (method/headers/url), pathname, handlerType, serverFnMeta (fn name when a server fn). The middleware result exposes response (status). (3) Context: next({context:{log, reqId}}) injects the request-scoped pino child into server-fn context (typed via GlobalServerRequestContext); ALSO wrap next() in AsyncLocalStorage.run({log, fields}, ...) so services/db deep in the stack append fields without prop-drilling. (4) In a finally after next(), emit logger.info({reqId, handlerType, method, pathname, fn, status, durationMs, ...fields}, 'request'). (5) reqId sourcing: prefer an inbound correlation header, else generate — reqId = request.headers.get('cf-ray') ?? request.headers.get('x-request-id') ?? crypto.randomUUID(). Reusing Cloudflare's cf-ray correlates app logs with CF edge logs (the app is CF-fronted); crypto.randomUUID is zero-dep (ULID/nanoid only if time-sortable ids are later wanted). Prereq: project has NO Start instance yet (no src/start.ts) — this bead must add createStart + register the global request middleware. NOT pino-http (that's Node req/res; Start uses web Request/Response) — hand-roll with a pino child.
notes: Builds on gf-fwi.13: the Start instance + global request middleware + minimal error logging are established there; THIS bead extends that same middleware into the full wide-events model (AsyncLocalStorage field accumulation + one canonical log line per request + reqId from cf-ray/x-request-id). OWNS 5xx-response logging: gf-fwi.13 logs THROWN errors, but Start's executeMiddleware resolves returned/thrown Responses (incl. 5xx) into next()'s result rather than throwing, so they bypass gf-fwi.13's catch (codex flagged this). gf-fwi.12 logs status per request, capturing those 5xx outcomes — do it here (not gf-fwi.13) to avoid double-logging. TRIGGER to promote to a pre-prod gate (make gf-fwi.4 depend on this): once server routes (createFileRoute server handlers) that RETURN Responses exist, the 5xx-Response gap becomes real and observability is incomplete without this. Until then, the app is server-fn-only and every failure is a thrown error that gf-fwi.13 already logs, so this stays a P3 enhancement, not a deploy gate. Coverage caveat: truly raw Nitro routes outside Start bypass request middleware; negligible for this app.
close_reason: Wide-events canonical-log-line middleware delivered: one structured 'request' line per request (reqId from cf-ray/x-request-id/uuid, pino child, method/path/handlerType/fn/status/durationMs + ALS-accumulated fields). emitRequestLog self-guarding (logging never changes request outcome); runInstrumented lifecycle extracted + unit-tested; request-context ALS (addRequestFields/getRequestLog). Owns 5xx-response logging (gf-fwi.13 gap). Replaced handle-request-error. Reviewed 2 iterations + post-loop + extraction re-review (codex + agents, all clean); 72 tests + build green, client bundle clean; smoke-verified end-to-end (router GET / -> one INFO line). Follow-ups: gf-fwi.14, gf-fwi.15.
